intro.text: This entry describes oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-29 (OZEMA29), a form of female infertility in which oocytes, zygotes or early embryos fail to develop normally. The causal gene and the reports defining this subtype are not recalled here.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-29 (OZEMA29) is a form of female infertility in which oocytes, zygotes or early embryos fail to develop normally.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous splicing variant (c.788 + 3A>G) in TBPL2 was identified in two unrelated families characterized by oocyte maturation defects.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes female infertility with oocyte maturation defects. It does not use the OZEMA29 designation and does not mention zygote or embryo arrest.

paragraphs.text: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) is a group of genetically different disorders that cause primary female infertility. Affected women have normal menstrual cycles and respond to ovarian stimulation. During assisted reproduction, however, their oocytes arrest at a stage of meiotic maturation, fail to be fertilized, or produce zygotes or embryos that arrest during early cleavage and cannot be transferred.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) is a group of genetically different disorders.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Only the title was supplied, and it says nothing about OZEMA being a genetically diverse group of disorders.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) causes primary female infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: A recurrent mutation in TBPL2 causes diminished ovarian reserve and female infertility.
checks.explanation: The title links the condition to female infertility, but it does not say 'primary' infertility or mention OZEMA as a group. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: Women affected by OZEMA have normal menstrual cycles.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Only the title was supplied. It does not mention menstrual cycles.

checks.claim: Women affected by OZEMA respond to ovarian stimulation.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Only the title was supplied. It does not mention response to ovarian stimulation. It mentions diminished ovarian reserve, which may not fit well with this claim.

checks.claim: During assisted reproduction, oocytes from women with OZEMA may arrest at a stage of meiotic maturation.
checks.evidence_quote: only two immature MI oocytes were obtained from the patients
checks.explanation: The patients' oocytes were immature metaphase I (MI) oocytes, which fits meiotic maturation arrest. However, the abstract does not describe arrest during assisted reproduction in general terms.

checks.claim: During assisted reproduction, oocytes from women with OZEMA may fail to be fertilized.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Only the title was supplied. It does not mention fertilization failure.

checks.claim: During assisted reproduction, oocytes from women with OZEMA may produce zygotes or embryos that arrest during early cleavage and cannot be transferred.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Only the title was supplied. It does not mention zygotes or embryos arresting during early cleavage.

paragraphs.text: OZEMA is genetically heterogeneous, and different numbered subtypes are caused by mutations in different genes. Examples include OZEMA1, caused by mutation in TUBB8, OZEMA2, caused by mutation in PATL2, and OZEMA3, caused by mutation in WEE2.

checks.claim: OZEMA is genetically heterogeneous, with different numbered subtypes caused by mutations in different genes.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Only the title was supplied. It does not discuss genetic heterogeneity or numbered subtypes.

checks.claim: OZEMA1 is caused by mutation in the TUBB8 gene.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The title mentions only TBPL2, not TUBB8 or OZEMA1.

checks.claim: OZEMA2 is caused by mutation in the PATL2 gene.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The title mentions only TBPL2, not PATL2 or OZEMA2.

checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The title mentions only TBPL2, not WEE2 or OZEMA3.
